courses.title: INTRODUCTION TO PUBLIC HEALTH SCIENCE
courses.instructor: Angela Christina Orefice, Michelle Lee Zulim-Clark, Michelle Marie Sheen
courses.description: Provides an introduction to the discipline of Public Health. Students will gain an understanding of the basic concepts and terminologies of public health, and the history and accomplishments of public health officials and agencies. An overview of the functions of various public health professions and institutions, and an in-depth examination of the core public health disciplines is covered. Topics of the discipline include the epidemiology of infectious and chronic disease; prevention and control of diseases in the community including the analysis of the social determinants of health and strategies for eliminating disease, illness and health disparities among various populations; community organizing and health promotion programming; environmental health and safety; global health; and healthcare policy and management. Transfer: CSU, UC. (Formerly HEED 210)

courses.description: Examines an introductory overview of U.S. social welfare, social work, and social institutions that deliver the provision of human support services. courses.title: CHICANX AND LATINX COMMUNITY PRACTICE
courses.description: Examines historical and contemporary efforts to address patterns of inequities affecting Chicanx and Latinx communities. Introduces key concepts for understanding equity, policy change, and community wellbeing among Chicanx and Latinx communities. Covers intergenerational trauma, medical exploitation, eugenics, intersectional disparities, barriers to accessing care, Latino Threat Narrative, cultural humility, advocacy, ethnic enclaves, and culturally responsive interventions. Pays special attention to the consequences of inequities in shaping community wellbeing. Advisory: ETHN 230 or ETHN 260. Transfer: CSU; UC. Same as ASHS 262.
